text:
Rafael Mendes: Dropping runbook draft for auto-rollback on SLO breach. Would love eyes esp on “what does oncall do after an auto-rollback fires” + what links/templates we should include.

Runbook draft (Confluence): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/SRE/Runbook+-+Auto-rollback+on+SLO+breach

Open Qs:
1) Do we page on every auto-rollback event or only on failures / repeated events?
2) After rollback triggers, what’s the minimum verification checklist before we close it out?
3) Where should the runbook point folks: dashboards, logs, ticket templates?

Miles Thornton: :eyes: reading now. I’d add a very explicit “stabilize + verify” checklist right after the incident-bot ping.

Proposed steps:
- Confirm traffic split actually reverted (Console > Rollouts page or routing config diff)
- Confirm current active version == previous stable (not just “canary set to 0%”)
- Check if rollback executor succeeded or we’re in a “rollback attempted” partial state
- Check evaluator decision trace for which SLO breached + window + baseline compare

Also: add a “don’t immediately reattempt rollout” warning unless you’ve validated monitors aren’t lying.

Kira Thompson: Agree on checklist. Runbook is a bit narrative rn; for oncall I’d put a TL;DR block at top with 6 bullets.

Also we should include the exact ticket template link we want people to use. Otherwise we get 10 different incident formats.

Allison Grant: For links, please point to the standard dashboards, not a saved personal view.

Suggested:
- Rollout SLO dashboard (latency + error) base: https://grafana.redwoodinference.com/d/rollout-slo/rollout-slo
- “Monitor health / staleness” panel: https://grafana.redwoodinference.com/d/rollout-slo/rollout-slo?viewPanel=42
- Rollout-controller internal metrics (monitor fetch errors, evaluator lag): https://grafana.redwoodinference.com/d/rollout-controller/rollout-controller

And call out which variables to set: `route`, `model`, `region`, `tier`, `candidate_version`.

Benji Okafor: +1. One important nuance: evaluator can now emit `UNKNOWN` verdict when monitor is stale/unavailable (from the guardrail PR). Runbook should tell oncall what to do in that case:
- If `UNKNOWN`, DO NOT treat it as breach confirmation
- Check `rollout_controller_monitor_fetch_errors_total` and `rollout_controller_monitor_last_success_ts`
- If monitors are down, we’re intentionally not rolling back (or we rollback only if policy says fail-closed) — oncall needs to know which mode this tenant/policy is in.

Maybe add a section “If verdict is UNKNOWN” with explicit next action: investigate monitoring outage, consider pausing further rollouts, but don’t thrash versions.

Sean Gallagher: Paging policy: we should NOT page for every successful auto-rollback. That becomes noise fast.

My take:
- Create ticket for every auto-rollback event (for follow-up + pattern tracking)
- Page only if:
  a) rollback fails (executor error / stuck),
  b) rollback triggers >N times in M mins (flapping),
  c) customer impact continues after rollback (latency still bad / error still high),
  d) rollback triggers across many tenants at once (possible regional/systemic incident)

We should codify the thresholds (N/M) in the runbook and align with incident-bot routing.

Hannah Rivera: Fwiw incident-bot message for auto-rollback already includes links (rollout page + dashboard + runbook). But today it’s not obvious what to click first.

Can we standardize the order in the runbook to match the notification?
- 1) Rollout page (see which version + traffic split)
- 2) SLO dashboard (confirm breach / recovery)
- 3) “Decision trace” logs (why did we do it)

Also, the Slack notification includes an “Open ticket” shortcut; we should make sure it points at the right template.

Connor O'Brien: +1 on template. Also please include the “disable auto-rollback” escape hatch with the exact flag name + where it lives.

We’ve been using:
- Feature flag: `rollout_auto_rollback_slo_enabled`
- Per-tenant override in config service

Oncall-friendly guidance: “If you suspect false positives, pause policy rather than hot-editing thresholds during incident.”

Rafael Mendes: Super helpful. For ticket template, would this work?
- Jira template: https://jira.redwoodinference.com/secure/CreateIssue!default.jspa?project=INC&issuetype=Incident&template=auto-rollback-slo

Fields we want prefilled:
- Tenant
- Route
- Model/version (candidate + prior stable)
- Region/tier
- Breach type (p95 latency / 5xx)
- Rollback result (success/failure)
- Links: rollout page + Grafana + decision trace query

Miles Thornton: Yep. Also add a “post-rollback validation window” section.

Something like:
- Watch for 10–15 min after rollback
- Confirm SLO back within threshold AND trending stable
- If not recovered, this is likely not the candidate model regression (could be capacity/region/network) → escalate as normal incident.

That helps prevent folks from assuming rollback fixes everything.

Allison Grant: For decision trace query link: do we have a stable log filter yet? If yes, put the exact query string in the runbook.

E.g. in logs UI:
`service=rollout-controller event=auto_rollback_decision tenant=<TENANT> rollout_id=<ID>`

If not stable, at least provide the fields to search.

Benji Okafor: We do. Query pattern:
`k8s.container=rollout-controller AND json.event="slo_evaluation" AND json.rollout_id="<rollout_id>"`

Also note: there’s a second event for executor:
`json.event="rollback_execute"` with `idempotency_key`.

Kira Thompson: Can we add a tiny “common failure modes” section?
- Monitor label mismatch (route/model/region labels missing) → verdict wrong/UNKNOWN
- Low traffic → min-traffic guardrail blocks rollback (explain what “blocked” looks like)
- Cooldown active → repeated breaches won’t trigger immediate rollback

Those are the first things someone new will trip over.

Sean Gallagher: + add “when to escalate to platform vs observability”. Simple rule of thumb:
- If metrics look wrong / missing / stale → observability oncall
- If executor fails / traffic split doesn’t revert → control plane oncall
- If SLO still bad after rollback but monitors seem fine → broader incident (SRE)

Rafael Mendes: Great. I’ll update runbook with:
- TL;DR checklist
- Paging vs ticketing criteria (w/ flapping threshold placeholder)
- Links to Grafana dashboards + log queries
- Explicit UNKNOWN verdict handling
- Ticket template link + required fields
- Escape hatch for pausing/disabling auto-rollback

If anyone has strong opinions on flapping threshold default (e.g. 2 rollbacks / 30 min?) reply here.

Miles Thornton: I’d start with 2 rollbacks / 60 min for paging. Below that ticket-only.

(reacted with :thumbsup:)

Sean Gallagher: 2/60 seems reasonable. We can tune after game day.

incident-bot: Reminder: If you update oncall runbooks, please add/verify the runbook URL in alert annotations for `AutoRollbackTriggered` and `RollbackExecutorFailed`.
